 1                    I.   INTRODUCTIONS AND QUALIFICATIONS

 2   Q1.   PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 3   A.    My name is James A. Schichtl. My business address is 100 N. Stanton Street,

 4         El Paso, Texas 79901.

 5

 6   Q2.   HOW ARE YOU EMPLOYED?

 7   A.    I currently serve as the Vice President of Customer and Regulatory Solutions for

 8         El Paso Electric Company ("EPE" or "Company"). I have served as an EPE Vice

 9         President in charge of a range of responsibilities since June 2016.

10

11   Q3.   PLEASE SUMMARIZE YOUR EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND.

12   A.    I graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering in 1987 from

13         the University of Texas at El Paso, where I also studied graduate level finance,

14         economics, and econometrics. Throughout my career at EPE, I have attended and

15         presented material for numerous seminars and workshops related to cost of service,

16         rate and program design, and regulation.

17

18   Q4.   PLEASE SUMMARIZE YOUR PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE.

19   A.    Prior to joining EPE in February 2012, I spent 18 years in various regulatory

20         functions at Southern California Edison Company ("SCE"), 12 of those years in a

21         managerial capacity.     As Manager of Pricing Design and Research, I was

 5         efforts at the California Public Utilities Commission ("CPUC").

11         Manager, responsible for the production, filing, and execution of regulatory

12         applications before both the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission

13         ("Commission" or "NMPRC") and the Public Utility Commission of Texas

14         ("PUCT").

15

16   Q5.   PLEASE DESCRIBE YOUR CURRENT RESPONSIBILITIES WITH EPE.

17   A.    As Vice President of Customer and Regulatory Solutions, I am responsible for the

18         oversight and direction of EPE’s Load Research & Data Analytics, Rate Research,

19         and Regulatory Case Management groups. Load Research performs load research,

20         data analysis and forecasting functions. Rate Research encompasses EPE’s rate

21         research function, jurisdictional and class cost of service studies, rate design

 2         Case Management group coordinates and oversees regulatory filings made by EPE

 3         with the PUCT, the NMPRC, and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission

 4         ("FERC"), and local municipal regulators. My job duties require knowledge of the

 5         statutory and regulatory requirements of each jurisdiction.           I was assigned

 6         responsibility for the Customer Care and Meter and Field Services groups in 2025.

 7         Customer Care includes EPE’s billing, customer contact, and collections groups.

 8         The Meter and Field Services group handles AMI meter installations, other field

 9         services, and investigates energy diversion.     Up until that time, I was also

10         overseeing the Company’s Market Development and Resource Management

11         Department in 2024. In my role as Vice President of Customer and Regulatory

12         Solutions, I continue to regularly coordinate with that department.

13

14   Q6.   HAVE     YOU      PREVIOUSLY         PRESENTED         TESTIMONY           BEFORE

15         REGULATORY BODIES?

16   A.    Yes, I have previously filed testimony with and testified before the NMPRC,

17         PUCT, CPUC, and FERC.

18

19   Q7.   WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY?

20   A.    My testimony provides an overview of EPE, its operations, and its strategic goals

21         for a robust energy transition to achieve New Mexico’s decarbonization mandates

 4         structure. Finally, my testimony highlights the benefits to customers from EPE’s

5          continued investment in infrastructure upgrades, smart technology rollouts, and

6          renewable resource integration.

 4   Q9.   PLEASE DESCRIBE THE IMPACT ON EPE AND THE SERVICE

 5         TERRITORY OF THE ACQUISITION OF THE COMPANY BY IIF IN

 6         2020.

 7   A.    On March 11, 2020, the Commission issued a Final Order in Case

 8         No. 19-00234-UT approving the acquisition of EPE by Sun Jupiter Holdings LLC,

 9         an indirect, wholly-owned subsidiary of IIF US Holding 2 LP, one of three limited

10         partnerships that constitute the "Infrastructure Investments Fund" ("IIF"). IIF is a

11         long-term private investment fund that invests capital provided predominantly by

12         institutional investors (such as pension funds and insurance companies) in

13         infrastructure companies in developed countries.

14                 Access to the capital needed to maintain a safe reliable system in

15         New Mexico and to enable growth has been enhanced by IIF equity infusions,

16         which support IIF’s focus on economic development in the region. IIF’s focus on

17         economic development in our region has also been critical, starting with the $20

18         million development fund IIF established in New Mexico with the acquisition of

19         EPE.

 1   Q10. WHAT ARE EPE’S KEY STRATEGIC GOALS?

 2   A.   EPE’s mission and vision are to transform the energy landscape and power

 3        economic growth, innovation, and prosperity in our region. EPE has developed and

 4        evolved five strategic anchors over the last five years to support those goals.

 5

 6   Q11. PLEASE DISCUSS EPE’S ANCHORS AND INITIATIVES THAT

 7        UNDERLIE THE COMPANY’S STRATEGIC PLAN.

 8   A.   EPE’s five strategic anchors focus on improving customer satisfaction, supporting

 9        growth, leveraging technology, advancing environmental goals, and fostering a

10        culture of excellence.

12        EPE will simplify customer processes and improve the overall customer

13        experience. The Company aims to maintain high reliability, affordability, and

14        transparency by improving construction management, outage scheduling,

15        cybersecurity, and technology deployment. Affordability efforts include process

16        streamlining, technology adoption, and fuel cost reduction. External partnerships

17        will support economic growth and positive regulatory outcomes.

18        Serve Growth

19        EPE is focused on delivering solutions to serve large customers and to improve the

20        customer mix to the benefit of the entire system. Strategic partnerships will drive

21        growth by securing generation and grid resources, replacing retiring generation, and

 1                           III.   STRATEGIC OVERVIEW

 2   Q12. PLEASE DESCRIBE THE ISSUES AND DEMANDS CURRENTLY

 3        FACING ELECTRIC UTILITIES IN THE UNITED STATES.

 4   A.   The electric utility industry is experiencing generational structural change driven

 5        by electrification, decarbonization mandates, technology shifts, and new load

 6        growth.   From an engineering and regulatory perspective, the sector faces

 7        simultaneous system expansion, operational complexity, and evolving regulatory

 8        frameworks. I would categorize the challenges as –

 9           1. Rapid Load Growth and Electrification

10           2. Transmission Expansion and Interregional Coordination

11           3. Reliability, Resilience, and Extreme Weather

12           4. Financial and Capital Market Pressures

13           5. Distributed Energy Resources and Grid Modernization

14           6. Decarbonization and Resource Transition

15               Many of these challenges are familiar from the last decade, but the potential

16        load growth attributable to extremely large load customers, primarily data centers,

17        has changed the nature and urgency of the other issues. For example, rapid growth

18        from large customers and the attendant economic benefits increase financial

19        pressures and challenge decarbonization and resource transition initiatives. In

20        addition, in the background for many of these challenges are near-term supply chain




                                              10
                                         Amended Filing
                                EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
                                   DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                                    JAMES A. SCHICHTL




1         issues constraining new generation and transmission capacity expansion. These

2         challenges all may contribute to increased costs for the system.

3

4    Q13. HOW      DO     THOSE       ISSUES        AND   DEMANDS         IMPACT        EPE’S

5         OPERATIONS IN NEW MEXICO?

6    A.   Over the last five years, the most critical concerns have been decarbonization and

7         the transition to clean resources, electrification, distributed energy resources

 8        ("DER") and grid modernization, and transmission. The energy transition and

 9        renewable portfolio standards ("RPS") have dominated the conversation. Resource

10        planning and procurement have been diverging between EPE’s jurisdictions due to

11        very different state policy objectives, and EPE has been successful in meeting RPS

12        requirements and would expect to continue that for normal, historical growth. But

13        the large load imperative of just the last two years upends the status quo.

14

15   Q14. WHY IS THAT?

16   A.   EPE’s peak demand in New Mexico is about 500 MW. Just one large load customer

17        could double or triple EPE’s jurisdictional peak and severely complicate RPS

18        compliance (especially given the energy intensive nature of data center). Large

19        loads in New Mexico represent generational economic development opportunities,

20        but they require rapid resource development, transmission, and dispatchable (likely

21        gas) resources. Serving those customers, which may require significant future



                                               11
                                         Amended Filing
                                EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
                                   DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                                    JAMES A. SCHICHTL




1         capital investment, also introduces new financial and regulatory issues. In this case,

2         EPE is proposing new large load tariffs designed to recover the costs associated

3         with serving these customers. Importantly, service under the new tariffs also

4         requires an Energy Service Agreement designed to ensure other customers and EPE

5         are protected from the severe financial implications that could result from service

6         to customers requiring significant system investment.

7

8    Q15. IS EPE ON TRACK TO COMPLY WITH ITS NEAR AND LONG-TERM

9         RPS OBLIGATIONS UNDER THE RENEWABLE ENERGY ACT?

10   A.   Yes. EPE exceeded the 40 percent RPS requirement in 2025 and expects to

11        continue to meet or exceed the renewable and clean energy requirements as they

12        increase to 50 percent in 2030 and beyond. In 2016, EPE was the first, and so far

13        only, New Mexico utility to exit coal generation, and the Company continues to

14        add significant amounts of solar generation and battery storage. EPE is confident

15        the Company will reach full compliance with New Mexico policy requirements

16        while pursuing its own Company-wide sustainability goals.

17               The long-term picture is more complicated. Renewable resource additions,

18        which just two years ago dominated generation capacity growth in the United

19        States, have become more complicated and expensive with supply chain and tariff

20        issues, as well as swings in federal policy. Renewable Energy Act compliance,

2         retail energy sales increase substantially with new large load customers.

3

4    Q16. WHAT IS EPE DOING TO MODERNIZE AND BUILD ITS GRID TO

 5        SUPPORT GROWTH, SYSTEM RELIABILITY AND RESILIENCE, AND

 6        TO INTEGRATE RENEWABLE RESOURCES?

 7   A.   EPE was the first utility in New Mexico to utilize the Grid Modernization statute

 8        to implement advanced metering. With completion of the project in 2025, EPE has

 9        significant technology at the customer end of the distribution system to enable new

10        pricing options and demand response programs. EPE witness Omar Gallegos

11        details the three components of the transmission and distribution plant investment

12        included in this case – (1) organic, or normal, growth, (2) the interconnection of

13        renewable energy resources, and (3) reliability investments. The last category

14        includes wildfire mitigation investments as well as technology and grid

15        enhancements with substations designed for improved outage mitigation and

16        restoration.

17

19        TECHNOLOGIES TO DEFER OR REPLACE NEW SUPPLY-SIDE

20        INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS?

 8                           IV.     OVERVIEW OF EPE’S APPLICATION

 9   Q18. WHEN WAS EPE’S LAST RATE CASE AND WHAT WAS THE RESULT?

10   A.        Shortly after EPE’s 2020 acquisition by IIF was approved by the Commission, EPE

11             filed an application for revision of its retail rates in Docket No. 20-00104-UT. The

12             timing of EPE’s required filing was pursuant to a Commission order extending back

13             to EPE’s exit from the Four Corners Power Plant in 2016 in Docket

14             No. 15-00109-UT. EPE requested a revenue increase of $7.354 million, 6.1 percent

15             over existing base revenues, based on a requested ROE of 10.4 percent. In its order

16             issued on June 23, 2021, the Commission adopted a decrease of $3.3 million with

17             an ROE of 9 percent, which at the time was the among the lowest in the country.

18             EPE appealed the order in the case and was ultimately granted relief on several

19             issues. 1 The last time a base rate increase was authorized for EPE was by final

 4   Q19. WHY IS EPE FILING THIS RATE CASE AT THIS TIME?

 5   A.   The issuance of the final order in EPE’s last rate case was a demarcation point for

 6        EPE. Completion of the acquisition of EPE occurred on July 20, 2020, and the

 7        Company began a transition of management and mission going forward under new

 8        ownership. One distinct difference in operations of the Company is the increased

 9        capital investment in facilities serving the EPE system and New Mexico. As

10        explained in the testimony of EPE witness Richard Gonzalez, capital investment by

11        EPE has increased over the last five years and is expected to continue and even

12        increase over the next five years.        These investments are critical to the

13        modernization and continued reliability of EPE’s system as well as expanding the

14        Company’s ability to continue supporting economic development in the region.

15

16   Q20. PLEASE PROVIDE AN OVERVIEW OF THE REVENUE REQUIREMENT

17        REQUESTED IN THIS CASE.

18   A.   EPE is requesting an annual revenue requirement increase of $70.7 million, which

19        represents a 50.5 percent increase over current base revenues. The primary drivers

20        for the requested increase are an increase in Net Plant in Service of $274.4 million,

21        which contributes to the proposed rate base increase of $260.2 million.

 1   Q21. ARE THERE OTHER FACTORS DRIVING THE INCREASED CAPITAL

 2        INVESTMENT?

 3   A.   Yes.    Over the period corresponding to the time of EPE’s last case to

 4        today – roughly 2020 through 2025, the cost of goods required in utility

 5        construction have increased 35 percent to 60 percent. The well-known drivers over

 6        that period are the COVID-19 epidemic, the war in Europe, and significant supply

 7        chain disruptions. Significant cost increases for many of the inputs necessary for

 8        construction and operation of utility plant magnify the total cost of EPE’s

 9        investments and the resulting rate base. The stacked structural shocks across supply

10        chains, energy markets, labor, and capital costs have driven the Producer Price

11        Index higher over this period and many of these drivers are structural and persistent.

12

13   Q22. IS THE REQUESTED REVENUE REQUIREMENT NECESSARY FOR

14        EPE TO PROVIDE SAFE AND RELIABLE SERVICE?

15   A.   Yes. As EPE’s testimony supports, the capital investments and expenses reflected

16        in the proposed revenue requirement are prudent and essential for the safe and

17        reliable operation of EPE’s system. One notable example is the investment in

18        transmission EPE has made to replace wood structures with steel in fire-prone areas

19        of New Mexico in order to protect EPE’s import capabilities. As EPE witness

20        Gallegos testifies, this investment has already protected against fire exposure in

21        2025.

 2   Q23. PLEASE      DESCRIBE        EPE’S    REQUESTED        CHANGES        TO      THE

 3        AUTHORIZED ROE AND CAPITAL STRUCTURE.

 4   A.   As explained by Company expert witness Jennifer Nelson, EPE is requesting an

 5        ROE of 10.7 percent. EPE is also proposing the Commission authorize an equity

6         and debt capital structure, 55.5 percent and 44.5 percent, based on actual

 7        percentages as of the end of the Test Year Period.

 8

 9   Q24. WHAT IS THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE REQUESTED ROE AND

10        CAPITAL STRUCTURE ON EPE’S ABILITY TO MEET ITS STRATEGIC

11        GOALS, INCLUDING THE CLEAN ENERGY TRANSITION AND GRID

12        MODERNIZATION STRATEGIES??

13   A.   A reasonable ROE and capital structure are essential to enable EPE to continue

14        investing at the pace the Company deems necessary to meet its goals, but also to

15        maintain healthy credit ratings, as EPE witness Richard Gonzalez explains.

16

17                              V.     AFFORDABILITY

18   Q25. WHAT IS THE ANTICIPATED IMPACT OF EPE’S PROPOSED NEW

19        RATES ON LOCAL ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT AND CUSTOMER

20        AFFORDABILITY?

                                         Amended Filing
                                EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
                                   DIRECT TESTIMONY OF

 1   A.   EPE’s proposed increase represents a significant reorienting of rates in several

 2        ways. The most obvious is the system average increase required to move EPE to

 3        full cost recovery. This is primarily the result of incorporating the significant

 4        investments EPE has made to the New Mexico system over the last six years, and

 5        the industry and economic changes that have occurred over that time. EPE’s past

 6        and planned investments will enable future economic growth, especially with

 7        potential large customer growth.

 8                EPE’s proposal to move to cost-based rates for all rate classes over two

 9        phases balances the need to remove subsidies by commercial customers with
